text:
natalie: FYI I'm getting multiple reports that the usage charts on the Console are stuck on a spinner. Seen by customers in eu-west1 and us-west. Network tab shows analytics-api returning 500 sometimes and long timeouts other times.

devin: ugh, seeing this too. Repro steps from a customer: 1) open /console/usage 2) select 90d range 3) toggle group-by -> spinner. Repro locally with the same query params.

samira: Can you paste the failing request/response? Suspect long-tail aggregation hitting downstream store.

natalie: here's the request from Chrome devtools:

Request: POST https://analytics-api.redwood.internal/v1/query
Body: {"range":"90d","metric":"tokens_per_org","group_by":["model","team"]} 
Response: 500 (internal). No body, connection closed after ~18s.

ops-bot: Deploy 2025-02-22T09:14:03 by @lina to analytics-api succeeded :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Recent error spike: analytics-api 500s increased from 0.2% to 8.6% at 09:12 UTC. Top trace: query fanout -> join timeout.

lina: I'm on it. Looking at the service traces now — a handful of slow queries are blocking the aggregator's worker pool. Seems to be high-cardinality group-bys that expand into many shard reads.

marc: Could this be related to the KV cache evictions we rolled yesterday? I saw a partial cache purge during the deploy window but didn't think it'd surface as 500s.

lina: Good catch. Metrics show cache hit rate fell from 94% -> 62% around the same time. If many cache misses cause synchronous calls to the datastore, it could exhaust the query concurrency and trigger 500s.

devin: Quick repro log (on a local run w/ sampling):
```
[2025-02-22T09:12:05Z] query_id=xy123 start fanout=240 shards
[2025-02-22T09:12:25Z] shard_read timeout after 10s (retries exhausted)
[2025-02-22T09:12:26Z] aggregator: worker_pool exhausted -> respond 500
```

samira: If worker_pool exhaustion is the cause, we can either increase pool size (short term) or add a guard for very-high-cardinality group-bys to return a 429 or a lighter-weight result. Which is preferred?

lina: For immediate mitigation I'll enable a soft-limit on fanout=100 in analytics-api and add early short-circuit for group_by cardinality above 200. That should stop the panics and reduce 500s. Longer term we should add prefix/KV caching for grouped aggregates.

natalie: Sounds good. Can you also post the rollout plan here so Support can update affected customers?

lina: Plan: 1) push config change to staging (09:40) 2) smoke test with large query (09:50) 3) apply to prod with 5% canary (10:05) 4) monitor error-rate and latency for 30m, then expand to 100% if stable. I'll pin the config diff shortly.

devin: For customers already hit, suggested workaround: reduce the time-range or remove the group_by. Also try the 'summary' view which uses pre-aggregated counters. I'll draft a templated message.

marc: I pushed a quick metric dashboard: https://dashboards/redwood/analytics-api/errors?from=now-1h showing the spike. Sharing with SRE.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-0222-001 - Console graphs failing due to analytics-api fanout overload. Assigned: @lina, @devin.

samira: After applying soft-limit to staging, the large query returned 200 within 1.9s with a truncated group_by summary. Pushing to canary now.

natalie: Great. Support will notify customers and follow-up if any still see issues. Thanks all :thumbsup:

lina: Update 10:28 UTC — canary looks healthy, 500s down to 0.3%, rolling to 100% now. Will follow up with postmortem if root cause ties back to cache eviction bug.

devin: Please add the exact query hash to the postmortem so we can block or optimize it in model-specific dashboards.

natalie: Noted. Closing thread once rollback/pm draft is in.
